findings.description: The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port to the entire internet rather than restricting it to known administrative IP ranges.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. While a web server may need public HTTP access, it is served over plaintext (no HTTPS/443 or TLS termination configured), meaning all traffic to/from the server is unencrypted.

The security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no egress control and enabling potential data exfiltration or command-and-control communication if the instance is compromised.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is readable by anyone with EC2 describe-instance-attribute permissions, exposing long-lived credentials far beyond the intended audience.

The instance does not configure metadata_options to require IMDSv2 (token-based), leaving the legacy instance metadata service enabled which permits credential theft via SSRF vulnerabilities in the deployed application.
The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched here, increasing the internet-facing attack surface for what may not need to be public.
The subnet has map_public_ip_on_launch set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to any instance launched in this subnet, expanding the internet-facing attack surface unnecessarily.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true nor specify a KMS key, so the volume's data at rest is unencrypted by default.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving sensitive network traffic logs unencrypted at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing access controls / public access block
findings.description: The S3 bucket has no public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restricting access, and force_destroy is enabled, risking accidental exposure or deletion of the flow log archive containing sensitive network metadata.
